title: On Maddening Myth; Mirvish's Medea Provides A Home For A Hellish Woman

contact_edits.before: It's worth, though, going beyond the end. Medea escaped to Athens, courtesy of King Aegeus to whom she'd promised release from sterility. She came through and he had a son, Theseus, whose second wife Phaedra became a tragic heroine on her own account, falling in love with her stepson and causing both his death and her own. And Phaedra is a role that Connolly played at Stratford two decades ago and that McKenna is to play there this year. Myth is continuous. And inescapable. - Medea runs through Feb. 9 at the Canon Theatre. For more information, call 416-872-1212.
